title: Renal Tubular Acidosis: Distal Type 1, Proximal Type 2, Fanconi and Type 4
subject: ss-paediatric-nephrology
module: Tubulopathies, Polycystic Kidney Disease and Ciliopathies

steps.say: All forms of renal tubular acidosis share a non-gap hyperchloremic metabolic disturbance.
steps.tx: Identify tubular bicarbonate and proton transport defects by noting the **Shared hallmark of normal anion gap acidosis** on chemistry panels. All forms of renal tubular acidosis present with normal serum anion gap (hyperchloremic) metabolic acidosis, where the calculated Serum Anion Gap = Na - (Cl + HCO3) remains strictly between 8 and 12 mEq/L, reliably separating tubular acidification pathology from organic ketoacidosis or lactic acidemia.

left.title: Renal Tubular Acidosis
points: Normal serum anion gap (8 to 12 mEq/L)
Defective tubular H+ excretion or HCO3 reabsorption

right.title: High Anion Gap Acidosis
points: Accumulation of unmeasured fixed organic anions
Ketoacidosis, lactic acidosis, or inborn metabolic errors

steps.say: Distal tubular failure manifests as inability to excrete protons despite systemic acidemia.
steps.tx: Evaluate cortical collecting duct function recognizing the **Distal RTA Type 1 alpha-intercalated defect** in children presenting with failure to thrive. Type 1 (distal) RTA is caused by failure of alpha-intercalated cells to excrete H+ ions into tubular lumens (mutations in SLC4A1/AE1, or ATP6V1B1/ATP6V0A4 associated with sensorineural deafness), resulting in persistent inability to acidify urine below pH 5.5 despite severe systemic acidemia.

vis.alt: Collecting duct proton pump failure with stones and acidosis in distal RTA.
vis.caption: Distal RTA: failed proton secretion, stones and acidosis. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Urine net charge reflects impaired medullary ammonium synthesis and distinguishes renal from bowel losses.
steps.tx: Calculate urinary net charge to confirm a **Positive urine anion gap in distal RTA** during workup. The Urine Anion Gap calculated as [U_Na + U_K - U_Cl] is positive in distal RTA (indicating severely impaired urinary ammonium NH4+ excretion by collecting duct intercalated cells), whereas it is strongly negative in gastrointestinal bicarbonate loss from diarrhea where renal ammonium generation remains fully intact.

vis.title: Urine Anion Gap Diagnostic Interpretation
rows: Low urinary NH4+ excretion from failing tubules
High urinary NH4+ paired with chloride excretion

steps.say: Alkaline urinary pH and profound hypocitraturia precipitate extensive calcium phosphate crystal deposition.
steps.tx: Examine renal parenchyma by ultrasound detecting **Nephrocalcinosis and hypocitraturia in Type 1** disease early. Chronic systemic acidosis stimulates proximal tubular citrate reabsorption, causing severe hypocitraturia and hypercalciuria; alkaline luminal urine precipitates insoluble calcium phosphate salts, producing bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis, recurrent nephrolithiasis, and crippling hypophosphatemic rickets.

steps.say: Proximal reabsorption failure lowers the tubular bicarbonate threshold and triggers generalized transporter collapse.
steps.tx: Assess proximal convoluted tubular transport to diagnose **Proximal RTA Type 2 and Fanconi syndrome** in young infants. Type 2 (proximal) RTA reflects defective proximal bicarbonate threshold reabsorption (< 15-18 mEq/L) via SLC4A4 (NBCe1), frequently occurring as part of generalized Fanconi syndrome characterized by glucosuria, aminoaciduria, phosphaturia, and uricosuria (seen in cystinosis, Lowe syndrome, galactosemia, and tyrosinemia).

vis.caption: RTA types 1, 2 and 4 by defect site. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Bicarbonate infusion titration quantifies proximal tubular wasting and distinguishes type one from type two.
steps.tx: Execute diagnostic bicarbonate loading to calculate **Fractional excretion of bicarbonate in Type 2** variants. When serum bicarbonate is normalized to 24 mEq/L via intravenous bicarbonate infusion, proximal RTA shows massive fractional excretion of bicarbonate (FE_HCO3) > 15-20% due to exceeded proximal threshold capacity, whereas in pure distal RTA the fractional excretion remains < 5%.

left.title: Proximal RTA (Type 2)
points: Massive bicarbonaturia when serum HCO3 reaches 24 mEq/L

steps.say: Specific lysosomal depletion therapy rescues visual and renal function in infantile cystinosis.
steps.tx: Initiate substrate depletion therapy targeting **Cystinosis and cysteamine therapy** upon diagnosing infantile Fanconi syndrome. Infantile nephropathic cystinosis, caused by autosomal recessive mutations in the CTNS gene encoding the lysosomal transporter cystinosin, is the leading monogenic cause of Fanconi syndrome; oral cysteamine at 1.3 g/m²/day and cysteamine eye drops deplete intralysosomal cystine crystals, preserving renal function and clearing corneal crystal deposits.

steps.say: Hyperkalemic tubular acidosis reflects impaired mineralocorticoid signalling and requires targeted electrolyte management.
steps.tx: Evaluate hyperkalemic non-gap acidosis by recognizing **Type 4 RTA hyperkalemic presentation** patterns in infancy. Type 4 RTA is characterized by hyperkalemia due to aldosterone deficiency or aldosterone resistance (pseudohypoaldosteronism Type 1: SCNN1A/B/G or NR3C2), treated with oral fludrocortisone, dietary potassium restriction, and sodium polystyrene sulfonate to normalize serum potassium and restore medullary ammonium generation.
